title: Radians and the Unit Circle
seo_title: Unit Circle Worksheet: Radians, Reference Angles, Exact Trig Values (Algebra 2) | 100 Questions
standard_text: Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.
meta_desc: Free Algebra 2 worksheet on radians and the unit circle: converting degrees and radians, coterminal and reference angles, exact sin, cos and tan, and sin² + cos² = 1. 100 questions.
key_big: π radians = 180°. On the unit circle, the point at θ is (cos θ, sin θ).
key_sub: Reference angles give the size; the quadrant gives the sign.
body_html:
How it works

A radian is the angle that cuts off an arc equal to the radius. π radians = 180°, so multiply by π/180 to change degrees to radians and by 180/π to change back.

On the unit circle (radius 1), the point at angle θ is (cos θ, sin θ), and tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ.

  • Use the reference angle (the acute angle to the x-axis) to get the size: 30°, 45° or 60° give 1/2, √2/2 and √3/2.
  • Use the quadrant to get the sign: in II only sin is positive, in III only tan, in IV only cos.
  • Pythagorean identity: sin² θ + cos² θ = 1.
Example

Find cos 210°.

Reference angle 30°, so |cos| = √3/2

Quadrant III: cos is negative

Answer: −√3/2

Example

sin θ = 3/5 in Quadrant II. Find cos θ.

cos² θ = 1 − 9/25 = 16/25

cos is negative in II

Answer: −4/5

Common mistakes

  • Using 180/π to change degrees to radians. Use π/180.
  • Swapping sine and cosine: sine is the y-coordinate.
  • Forgetting the sign from the quadrant.
  • Measuring the reference angle from the y-axis instead of the x-axis.

faq.q: How do you convert degrees to radians?
faq.a: Multiply by π/180. For example, 120° × π/180 = 2π/3.

faq.q: What are the coordinates on the unit circle?
faq.a: The point at angle θ is (cos θ, sin θ). The x-coordinate is cosine and the y-coordinate is sine.
The acute angle between the terminal side of an angle and the x-axis. It gives the size of the trig values.
sin²θ + cos²θ = 1. If you know one of sin θ or cos θ and the quadrant, you can find the other.
